claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

=== YOUR SITUATION PROFILE ===
You live in the UK.
You are inquiring about your 1 child:
  - Alex is 8 years old and lives with you.

Here are the exact details of your circumstances to use when answering the agent's questions:

Regarding Alex:
  - Claimant lives in the UK
  - Child is 8 (under 16)
  - Another claimant who lives with the child has priority
  - Child is not in local authority care
  - Child is not in hospital or residential accommodation
  - Child is not fostered
  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week
  - Child has not started an apprenticeship in England
  - Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit! Let me start by getting the first assessment question.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To get started, I need to know about the child or children you're claiming for.

**How old is the child (or the youngest child if you have multiple children)?**

Please let me know their age, as this will determine which path we follow in the eligibility assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I'd like to find out if I can claim Child Benefit. I have one child - Alex, who is 8 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Thank you for that information. So you have one child, Alex, who is 8 years old.

Since Alex is under 16 years old, this is excellent news as children under 16 automatically qualify on the age criterion. Now let me check the next requirement.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check another eligibility requirement:

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or is he not in paid work at all?**

Given that Alex is 8 years old, I expect he's not working, but I need to confirm this for the assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't work at all - he's only 8, he's still in primary school!

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's what I expected. So Alex is not in paid work and is in primary school. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check another requirement:

**Is Alex NOT receiving certain benefits in their own right, such as Employment and Support Allowance (ESA) or Universal Credit?**

In other words, is Alex not claiming these benefits for themselves?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't receive any benefits in his own name. He's just a child living at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's clear. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good progress! Now I need to check about apprenticeships:

**Is Alex in an apprenticeship, or is he not in an apprenticeship at all?**

Since Alex is 8 years old and in primary school, I'd expect he's not in an apprenticeship, but I need to confirm this for the assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in an apprenticeship - he's only 8 and in primary school!

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That confirms Alex is not in an apprenticeship. Let me move forward to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Now I need to check the residency requirements. The good news is that there are multiple paths that can satisfy this requirement - if **ANY** of these apply to you, you can proceed:

1. **Normally live in the UK**
2. **Settled status** under the EU Settlement Scheme
3. **Pre-settled status** and currently working (earning above the National Insurance threshold for 3 months)
4. **Pre-settled status** and actively seeking work (jobseeker for up to 91 days)
5. **Pre-settled status** with sufficient resources to support yourself and family
6. **Pre-settled status** and studying with sufficient resources
7. **Pre-settled status** as a family member of an EEA or Swiss national with right to reside
8. **Crown servant living abroad** in certain qualifying countries

**Which of these situations applies to you?** Or to put it simply: **Do you normally live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - we're in Manchester.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's exactly what we need. Since you normally live in the UK, you meet the residency requirements. Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check if you're responsible for Alex. Again, there are multiple ways this can be satisfied - if **ANY** of these apply, you meet this requirement:

1. **Living with the child** - You live with Alex
2. **Contributing to the child's upkeep** - You pay at least the same amount as Child Benefit towards their care (food, clothes, pocket money, housing, presents, etc.)
3. **Paying maintenance** - You make payments under a court order or agreement for the child's maintenance

**Which of these applies to you?** Or to put it simply: **Do you live with Alex and support him financially?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! So you live with Alex and support him - that clearly meets the responsibility requirement. Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check an important point:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or has anyone else claimed it for him previously?**

For example:
- Is the other parent claiming Child Benefit for Alex?
- Is another relative or guardian claiming for him?
- Has someone else been claiming and you're now taking over the claim?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, actually, Alex's other parent is already claiming Child Benefit for him, and Alex lives with them.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I see - that's an important detail! So Alex's other parent is currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex, and Alex actually lives with them, not with you.

Let me clarify the situation to make sure I have this right:

**Where does Alex live most of the time?** Does he live primarily with the other parent, or do you share custody where Alex spends significant time with both of you?

This is important because Child Benefit can only be claimed by one person, and it should be claimed by the person who is mainly responsible for looking after the child on a day-to-day basis.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex lives with his other parent full-time. I don't have him staying with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. So Alex lives full-time with the other parent, who is already claiming Child Benefit for him, and you don't have him staying with you.

Given this situation, since:
- Alex lives full-time with the other parent
- You are not responsible for Alex's day-to-day care and upkeep
- Another person is already claiming Child Benefit for Alex
- You don't meet the "responsibility" requirement (living with the child or contributing to their upkeep)

Let me navigate to the appropriate outcome.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I appreciate the clarification. However, I need to reconsider this based on the decision tree path I'm following. Let me ask:

**Is Alex in any of these special situations:**
- In hospital?
- In care (local authority care)?
- Being fostered?
- Or is he living in a normal family home with the other parent?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's living in a normal family home with his other parent.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for confirming. Let me proceed with this information.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I see we've reached the final check:

**Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words, the council is not contributing financially to support Alex's care or housing, correct?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's right, the council isn't paying anything - Alex just lives with his other parent in their normal home.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for that confirmation. Based on all the information you've provided, I can now give you my assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## Child Benefit Eligibility Assessment Result

**Result: NOT ELIGIBLE**

---

### Summary for Alex

I'm afraid you are **not eligible** to claim Child Benefit for Alex at this time.

**Why?**

While Alex meets many of the eligibility criteria (he's 8 years old, not working, not receiving benefits in his own right, and you live in the UK), **you do not meet the responsibility requirement** for Child Benefit.

Child Benefit can only be claimed by **one person** - the person who is responsible for the child's day-to-day care and upkeep. This responsibility is established through either:
- Living with the child and supporting them, OR
- Contributing substantially to their maintenance

Since Alex lives full-time with the other parent and you don't have him staying with you and are not contributing to his care or upkeep, **the other parent is the appropriate claimant**. The fact that the other parent is already claiming Child Benefit for Alex confirms this is the correct arrangement.

---

### What This Means

This is the correct situation for your family. Only one parent can claim Child Benefit for a child, and it should be the parent with whom the child lives and who is responsible for their day-to-day care. The other parent should continue their claim.

If your circumstances change in the future (for example, if Alex comes to live with you instead), you would be able to explore claiming Child Benefit at that point. You can contact HMRC to update them on any changes to custody or living arrangements.

**Reference:** https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/eligibility

Since Alex lives full-time with the other parent and you don't have him staying with you and are not contributing to his care or upkeep, you are not responsible for Alex. Additionally, the other parent is already claiming Child Benefit for Alex. Only one person can claim Child Benefit for a child.
